newsitem.title: USA: Astra USA ex-CEO Bildman pleads not guilty.
newsitem.headline: Astra USA ex-CEO Bildman pleads not guilty.

text.p: Lars Bildman, the former head of the U.S. subsidiary of Swedish firm Astra AB, pleaded not guilty in federal court on Wednesday to 35 criminal charges, including fraud and tax evasion.
U.S. Magistrate Judge Charles Swartwood ordered that Bildman, 51, remain in custody while the judge considered whether to release him on bail pending his trial in June.
The charges against Bildman also include conspiracy, mail fraud, wire fraud, filing false tax returns and interstate travel in the furtherance of prostitution.
Bildman was fired from Astra last year after reports of widespread sexual harassment and other abuses at the subsidiary, Astra USA.
U.S. Attorney Donald Stern told reporters after the hearing that the investigation into Astra was continuing and may lead to additional charges against Bildman or others.

If found guilty, Bildman faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine for each count of conspiracy, mail fraud, wire fraud and interstate travel. He faces up to three years and a $250,000 fine for each count of the tax charges.
Bildman is scheduled to go on trial on June 23 in Worcester, Mass.
